features.description: At a run's end the driver dry-applies the curator's ops on a copy of the base, writes memory-review-input.json (one item per op that would land, facts/<i> and rules/<n>), and runs one read-only `memory-review` session under the curator's deny list whose only kept output is memory-review.json; with nothing to review it runs no session and notes so.
steps: Written first and watched failing in a new slow file tests/checks/memory-review.sh (line 2 `# tier: slow`; its names in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt, LC_ALL=C sorted): a run with `STUB_CURATOR_OPS=three-ops STUB_MEMORY_REVIEW=hold` under MEMORY_POLICY=pr ends done with one `zz-memory-review-*.jsonl` transcript in its logs, a metrics.jsonl row whose role is `memory-review` after the `curator` row, a run.log line starting `memory review · ` after the `curator · ` line, harness-log.md's `memory review: session denied Bash(git push:*), Bash(gh:*)` note after the curator's notes and before the first `memory PR` note, and the review session's argv file in the stub's argv/ directory carrying `--disallowedTools` followed by exactly `Bash(git push:*)` and `Bash(gh:*)` (no other role's argv carries it besides the curator's).

In the same file: the run record's memory-review-input.json lists ids `facts/1`, `facts/2` (apply's order) and `rules/<n>` with the follow-up's `<run>/<n>` number from memory-result.json, each item with `op`, `file`, `section`, `anchor`, `text`, `why`, `from`, `base` and `after` paths under the scratch directory (`memory-base/` and `memory-after-facts/` or `memory-after-rules/`) and the gate's cap reading as `gotchas` and `lines` counted on the base; memory-review.json is kept in the run record; a run with `STUB_MEMORY_REVIEW_EDITS=1` (the stub reviewer also appends to CLAUDE.md and writes lib/review-hack.sh) has both edits reverted with one note `memory review: reverted edits (it is read-only): …`, its memory-review.json kept, and its record PR opened; a run with `STUB_CURATOR_OPS=proposal` (every op dropped or proposed) has no `memory-review` line in the stub's sessions.log, the note `memory review: nothing to review`, memory.json with `reviewed: 0` and `review: "nothing to review"`, and opens no facts PR, as today.

In the same file: `lib/prompt.sh <state dir> memory-review x` renders prompts/memory-review.md with the first line `# Memory review session`, naming memory-review-input.json, memory-review.json, the four questions (Q1 stated and recorded, Q2 no live referents with the `git grep -nF -e` form and its four exclusions, Q3 the cap and the anchor counted on the base, Q4 no duplicate: the same file under any heading, the user-level CLAUDE.md in the home directory's .claude read-only, and the declined rows of the ledger's memory-answers.jsonl read-only, so a declined rule restated under `## Gotchas` fails Q4), the thin rule (fewer than four rows fails the op), that it writes nothing but memory-review.json and that the driver denies push and gh, with no `{{` left (the curator's twin check in tests/checks/curator-run.sh stays where it is).

Written first in a new tests/unit/memreview.test.mjs (names in check-names.txt and check-names-fast.txt): lib/memreview.mjs `input` builds the items from one apply result's `applied` and `rules` in order, `facts/<i>` then `rules/<n>` with the result's numbers, each with the base and after paths and the cap reading passed in; from a result with empty `applied` and `rules` it returns an empty list; `node lib/memreview.mjs input <result.json> <base dir> <after-facts dir> <after-rules dir>` prints the list as one JSON document and exits 0.

The code: lib/memreview.mjs (new, usage header, `input` exported; `validate`, `verdicts` and `render` are R1-02's); prompts/memory-review.md; lib/config.sh `MEMORY_REVIEW_MODEL=opus` beside `CURATOR_MODEL` with the same comment shape, and its commented line in templates/user/config.sh and templates/project/config.sh; lib/driver.sh `memory_review()` (session `memory-review`, `MAX_TURNS=40 SESSION_BUDGET_USD=3`, `S_DENY=("${CURATOR_DENY[@]}")`, transcript `$LOGS/zz-memory-review-<HHMMSS>.jsonl`, `ro_rescue "$rstart" memory-review.json memory-review`, the `record MET append … memory-review …` row, the notes after the restrict); lib/record.sh `memory_pr` runs the dry apply on a copy of `$SCRATCH/memory-base` into `$SCRATCH/memory-after-facts` (tier 1 written by apply) and writes ruleTexts into `$SCRATCH/memory-after-rules`, writes `$RUN_DIR/memory-review-input.json` and commits it to the record branch before `rstart` is taken (restrict deletes an uncommitted new file), calls `memory_review` before the landing, and `memory_json` writes `reviewed` and `review`; lib/prompt.sh renders the `memory-review` role with the read-only where-things-go block as the curator's; tests/stub-claude.sh gains `# Memory review session` (writes memory-review.json from the run's memory-review-input.json: `hold` four holding rows per id, `evict-fails` fails `q: 2` of every anchored add and every delete with `ran` the `git grep -nF -e '<first backticked span of the anchor>' -- . ':!.harness/runs'` line and `saw` `7 files: …`, `thin` three rows for the first id, `none` no file, `bad` `{not json`, `limit` the captured rate-limit replay the other sessions use) and `STUB_MEMORY_REVIEW_EDITS`, both documented in the stub's header; `bash -n lib/driver.sh lib/record.sh lib/prompt.sh lib/config.sh tests/stub-claude.sh tests/checks/memory-review.sh` and `node --check lib/memreview.mjs` pass.

journal/decisions/2026-11-09-memory-reviewer.md is created (title, provenance, finding · choice · rejected) with R1-01's rows, each default marked *default*: Opus as the model behind a knob, the curator's deny list and bound, the gate first and the reviewer on what passed, tier 3 not reviewed, the skip with nothing to review, Q4's read of the declined answers rows (the brief's addition); docs/architecture.md gains `lib/memreview.mjs` and `prompts/memory-review.md` under Components, a Read-only sessions guard row for the reviewer, the REVIEW lines in the CURATOR step and `memory-review-input.json` and `memory-review.json` in the Memory curation state row; README.md's *Memory curator* paragraph gains a *Memory reviewer* paragraph.

`bash tests/run.sh memory-review` is timed once alone (`TEST_JOBS=1`) and the file's row (`memory-review` | slow | its seconds | over 30 s: stub runs) is added under the table in journal/decisions/2026-11-03-suite-tiers.md; `bash tests/run.sh memory-review curator-run` ends with every check passing (its `N/M checks passed` line).
`bash tests/run.sh --tier fast` ends with every check passing (its `N/M checks passed` line); the suite is green.

features.description: The reviewer's memory-review.json is validated and turned into one verdict per op (four questions, one row each; thin or missing rows fail), rendered as a `## Review` section with the verify's five-column evidence table in both PR bodies and memory.md, noted, counted in memory.json, and under MEMORY_POLICY=auto only held ops are committed and the facts PR merges only when the review ran and every committed op held.
steps: Written first in tests/unit/memreview.test.mjs: `validate <review.json> <input.json>` passes a file with four rows per input id and refuses, each naming the offending row, an `id` not in the input, a `q` of 5, a doubled `(id, q)`, a non-boolean `holds` and more than 4 × items rows; `verdicts <review.json> <input.json>` prints one JSON line `{reviewed, held, failed, ops: [{id, holds, reason}]}` holding an op whose four rows hold, failing one on its first failing row's `saw` with the question named (`… (q2)`), failing one with three rows as `review too thin (3 of 4 rows)` and one with no rows as `not reviewed`; `render <verdicts.json> <review.json>` prints `## Review`, one line per op (`- facts/1 holds`, `- facts/2 **fails**: <reason> (q2)`) and the table headed `| Op | Q | What you ran or read | What you saw | Holds |`, and `render` with a why and no files prints `## Review` with the one line `none: <why>`.

Written first in tests/unit/entries.test.mjs: `evidenceTable(rows, firstColumn)` is exported from lib/entries.mjs and renders the verify's five-column table, and `renderEntry`'s output for a verify entry with evidence is byte-identical to the fixture captured before the change (compare a hash or the first mismatching line, never deepEqual on the whole). Written first in tests/unit/curator.test.mjs: `apply … --verdicts <verdicts.json>` drops a failed op at its write with the reason `review: <reason> (<id>)` after every other step, so the duplicate-key choice stays as the full list made it (the earlier op of the same key does not land either); without `--verdicts` nothing is dropped by verdict; the landing with `--verdicts` equals the dry run's texts minus the failed ops' writes; `body … --review <section.md>` places `## Review` after the body's head and before *Applied*, and a body over BODY_MAX loses the review's table before any other part and never its one-line verdicts.

Written first in tests/checks/memory-review.sh (slow): `STUB_MEMORY_REVIEW=hold` on `three-ops` under MEMORY_POLICY=pr: both PR bodies (stub gh's body files) and the record's memory.md carry `## Review` with one `holds` line per op and the five-column table, harness-log.md has `memory review: 3 reviewed · 3 held · 0 failed` and memory.json has `reviewed`, `held`, `failed`, `review` (`ok`) and `merged_by` (null); `STUB_MEMORY_REVIEW=evict-fails` on `cap-evict` under pr: the eviction's line reads `**fails**` with the grep in its row, the facts commit on harness-memory/<run> still carries it, the note `memory review: facts/<i> fails: …` names it, and the PR is open with no `pr merge` in gh.log; the same under MEMORY_POLICY=auto: the facts commit lacks the failed op and holds the held one, the PR merges (`pr merge` of its URL in gh.log), memory.json reads `failed` 1 and `merged_by` `driver` with `dropped` equal to the pr run's, and `## Review` lists the failed op with its reason; `thin` fails the first op as thin and the rest hold; `none`, `bad` and `limit` each open the PR with `## Review` `none: <why>` (`the reviewer wrote no memory-review.json`, `memory-review.json invalid: …`, `the reviewer hit a limit`), one `memory review: none (<why>)` note, every op in the commit, and under auto no `pr merge` of that URL in gh.log and the note `memory PR: no review (<why>); not merged (MEMORY_POLICY=auto), left open · <url>`; a `harness continue` of the `none` run with `STUB_MEMORY_REVIEW=hold` and a new fact (tests/fixtures/memory/stub-fact-b.json) runs the review again and merges the reused PR; the rules PR's body carries the verdict and gh.log has no `pr merge` of its URL under either policy; a run on a project whose ledger memory-answers.jsonl holds a declined row for a rule the curator's ops restate under `## Gotchas` (`STUB_MEMORY_REVIEW=declined`, the stub reading the answers file the prompt names) fails that op's Q4 with `saw` naming `declined by Michael (<run>/<n>)` and under pr the PR body marks it `**fails**`.

tests/checks/curator-run.sh: the check `curator: its run.log line comes after the retro's, its notes before the record PR's` extends to the review's notes (the `memory review:` notes before the record PR's note) under a new name, the old name leaving tests/fixtures/check-names.txt in the same commit; the fixture's new names are LC_ALL=C sorted and the unit names are in check-names-fast.txt too; R1's added names against its budget of 35 are counted in the entry's `checks` field (over it: the reason there).

The code: lib/memreview.mjs `validate`, `verdicts`, `render` with the row caps from lib/entries.mjs; lib/entries.mjs `evidenceTable`; lib/curator.mjs `apply`'s `--verdicts <file>` flag (a flag like `--answers`, the follow-up's shape) with the `review:` drop reason and `body`'s `--review <file>` part and trim order; lib/record.sh `memory_pr`: the review validated (an invalid file refused whole with its first reason), verdicts written to `$SCRATCH/memory-verdicts.json`, the rendered section to `$SCRATCH/memory-review.md`, the landing apply given `--verdicts` under auto only, the no-review branch of the spec's §5 (no file, invalid, `MET limit`, non-zero exit or timeout: every op lands as under pr, `memory_merge` not called under auto, one note), `memory_json`'s `held`, `failed`, `review`, `merged_by`; lib/driver.sh `memory_review()` returns the why none; lib/summary.mjs `memoryOf` reads the keys and `memoryLine` ends `· review <held> held · <failed> failed` (nothing for a memory.json without `reviewed`); prompts/curator.md gains the two sentences (a reviewer checks every op against the record and the tree; an eviction, replace or delete of a line the tree still depends on fails, so a replace that keeps the subject beats an eviction); tests/stub-claude.sh gains `STUB_MEMORY_REVIEW=declined`; templates/user/config.sh and templates/project/config.sh's `MEMORY_POLICY` comment says auto merges only when the review ran and every committed op held; `bash -n lib/record.sh lib/driver.sh tests/stub-claude.sh tests/checks/memory-review.sh tests/checks/curator-run.sh` and `node --check lib/memreview.mjs lib/entries.mjs lib/curator.mjs lib/summary.mjs` pass; `grep -n memory_merge lib/record.sh` shows every call guarded by the review's status.

journal/decisions/2026-11-09-memory-reviewer.md gains R1-02's rows marked *default* (thin is a fail, not an escalation; failed ops land under pr and are dropped by verdict under auto, at the write, never removed from the input list; a reviewer that fails leaves the PR open under both policies; the rules PR carries every op with the verdict and is never merged) and the rejected list (raw ops reviewed; thin as escalation; failed ops dropped under pr; tier 3 reviewed); docs/architecture.md: the CURATOR step's REVIEW lines, the policy table's `auto` row reads `merged only when the review ran and every committed op held`, the PR table's bodies name `## Review`; README.md's *Memory reviewer* names the four questions and what lands by policy.

An Opus subagent reviews R1-02's diff (`git diff <merge-base with main> -- lib tests prompts`) for the four invariants (the reviewer writes nothing but memory-review.json; it never changes an op; no review, no merge; the follow-up's stand); Critical and Important findings are fixed RED→GREEN before the commit.
`bash tests/run.sh memory-review curator-run memory-branch` ends with every check passing (its `N/M checks passed` line).
`bash tests/run.sh --tier fast` ends with every check passing (its `N/M checks passed` line); the suite is green.

features.description: An Opus review of R1's whole diff against the four invariants, its findings fixed test-first, simplifications applied, the docs and the tiers table brought level; the review's file is docs/plans/2026-11-09-R1-review.md.
steps: `git diff $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main) -- lib prompts tests templates docs README.md > /tmp/harness/agent-harness/agent-harness-2026-11-09/R1.diff`; an Opus subagent reads the diff from that file (never the conversation) and writes docs/plans/2026-11-09-R1-review.md with its findings graded Critical, Important, Minor, on at least: every path that calls `memory_merge` (`grep -n memory_merge lib/record.sh`) is guarded by a review that ran and held every committed op; the reviewer session can write nothing the driver keeps but memory-review.json (the rescue, the revert, the deny list on its argv and on no role's but the curator's: `grep -n S_DENY lib/*.sh`); a failed op dropped by verdict cannot let an op the reviewer never saw land (the duplicate-key case in tests/unit/curator.test.mjs); `renderEntry` is unchanged (the byte-identical test); the stub's memory-review.json has the shape prompts/memory-review.md asks the real session for (the prompt's example and the stub's `hold` output compared field by field). A second round only when the first found something Critical.

Every Critical and Important finding is fixed with a failing check or unit test first (names into tests/fixtures/check-names.txt, and check-names-fast.txt for unit names; a replaced check's old name leaves in the same commit); Minor findings are fixed or listed in the review file with why not; simplification passes the reviewer names are applied.

docs/architecture.md and README.md are read against the code as merged (the role, the state files, the policy table, the guard row) and brought level; journal/decisions/2026-11-09-memory-reviewer.md lists R1's removed check names each with its successor (decisions/2026-11-03-trim's rule) and the milestone's count against the budget of 35; `bash tests/run.sh memory-review` is timed once more alone (`TEST_JOBS=1`) and the `memory-review` row in journal/decisions/2026-11-03-suite-tiers.md's table gets the new seconds beside the first.

`bash -n` on every shell file the fixes touched and `node --check` on every .mjs pass; `bash tests/run.sh memory-review curator-run memory-branch` ends with every check passing (its `N/M checks passed` line).
`bash tests/run.sh --tier fast` ends with every check passing (its `N/M checks passed` line); the suite is green.

features.description: The reviewer's cost, wall time and model reach memory.json, summary.json, the report's `Memory` row (`review 3 held · 0 failed · $0.42 · 4 min`), `Spend by role` and `Time`, and ledger/memory.jsonl's rows gain the review fields per tier; a reviewer dearer than its curator is one note.
steps: Written first in tests/unit/summary.test.mjs (names in check-names.txt and check-names-fast.txt): `build` reads memory.json's `review_cost_usd`, `review_s`, `review_model`, `reviewed`, `held`, `failed`, `review` and `merged_by` into summary.json's `memory` and leaves every review key out for a memory.json without `reviewed`; `memoryLine` ends `· review <held> held · <failed> failed · $<cost> · <n> min` for a reviewed summary, `· review none (<why>)` when `review` is not `ok` and nothing after `rules PR …` for a summary without `reviewed`; `reportRows`' `Spend by role` and `Time` list `memory-review` after `curator` when the summary has its cost; `memory-line` writes `reviewed`, `held`, `failed`, `review`, `failed_ids` (`["facts/2:q2"]`), `merged_by` and `review_cost_usd` into the facts row and the rules row of one run, each tier's counts from the input's `facts/*` or `rules/*` ids.

Written first in tests/checks/memory-review.sh (slow): after the `hold` run, `harness report <run>` prints the `Memory` row ending with the review tail and `Spend by role` with a `memory-review` line; the ledger's memory.jsonl has the review fields in both that run's facts row and its rules row; a run with `STUB_MEMORY_REVIEW_COST=2.5` (a new stub knob: the review session's `result` line's `total_cost_usd`, documented in the stub's header) gets the one note `memory review: cost $2.50 over the curator's $0.10` and a run with the default cost gets none.

features.description: `harness memory` shows each PR's held and failed columns (`unreviewed` for an old row), marks Michael's overrides from the row and gh's state, adds the `review:` tally line, and `harness memory <project>` ends with the `auto:` graduation line (window 8 reviewed facts PRs, at least 10 ops, 90 % held, at most one override); `memreview.mjs line` is the one text behind the harness-log.md note, the `Memory` row's counts and the future card.
steps: Written first in tests/unit/memory.test.mjs (or summary.test.mjs where `memoryView` is tested; names in check-names.txt and check-names-fast.txt): `memoryView` prints `held <h> · failed <f>` in a reviewed row's line and `unreviewed` for a row without the fields, ends a line `· override: merged against a fail` (state merged unchanged, `failed` > 0, `merged_by` not `driver`) or `· override: closed against a hold` (state merged edited or closed, `reviewed` > 0, `failed` 0), prints a driver-merged row with a fail as no override and a closed facts PR whose run has a declined row in the answers as no override, and adds the fourth tally line `review: held h · failed f · overrides o (merged against a fail m · edited or closed against a hold e) · unreviewed u`; `graduation(rows, states, answers, project)` returns `earned` for 8 reviewed facts PRs with 20 reviewed, 19 held, 0 overrides, `not yet` at 88 %, at 2 overrides and at 9 reviewed ops, `revisit` for a project on auto under 80 % held, and the line's wording `auto: not yet (held 7 of 8 · 88 % · overrides 1 of 6 reviewed PRs · window 8)`; `memreview.mjs line <verdicts.json> <memory.json>` prints `memory: facts <h> held · <f> failed (<id>: <reason>, q<n>) · rules <h> held · PR <url> · rules PR <url|none>` and the note and the card text are that one function's output.

Written first in tests/checks/memory-review.sh (slow): after the `hold`, `evict-fails` (pr) and `auto` runs on one project, `harness memory` lists each run's facts and rules lines with their columns, its `review:` tally counts the pr run's eviction as a fail and, once the stub gh's pr-N.merged marks that PR merged, as `merged against a fail`, and the auto run's merge as no override; `harness memory <project>` ends `auto: not yet (…)` naming `window 8`; without a project it prints no `auto:` line; the `evict-fails` run's `memory: facts …` note in harness-log.md equals `node lib/memreview.mjs line` run on that record's verdicts and memory.json. tests/checks/memory-branch.sh: `harness memory: the run's facts and rules PRs are a line each with its tier, then one tally line per tier; the facts PR merged unchanged after its merge` extends to the columns (`held`/`failed` or `unreviewed`) and the `review:` tally under a new name, the old leaving tests/fixtures/check-names.txt in the same commit.

The code: lib/summary.mjs or lib/memory.mjs (`memoryView`'s columns, the override reading with `merged_by` read where the override is decided, `graduation`, the tally); lib/memory.sh reads the ledger's memory-answers.jsonl for the declined-row rule and prints the `auto:` line last for a project (a project on auto by its config reads `revisit` under 80 %: a word, never a switch); lib/memreview.mjs `line`; lib/record.sh notes `line`'s output once after both PR notes (R1-02's counts note stays first); bin/harness's usage line for `harness memory` names the `auto:` line; `bash -n lib/memory.sh lib/record.sh bin/harness tests/checks/memory-review.sh tests/checks/memory-branch.sh` and `node --check lib/summary.mjs lib/memory.mjs lib/memreview.mjs` pass.
